label: D2 rare a1->S2 transition after a rewarded trial, early in the episode
explanation: About 81% of activation mass is at D2 on rare a1->S2 transitions (action input a1, state input S2). It never fires at D1, never when the reward input is 1 at that step, and never when the action input is a2. It is strongly tied to time in the episode: most activity is in trials 0-29, a little in 30-39, and none from trial 40 on. That makes it a time-gated rare-transition detector for a1 only. Restricting to steps where the previous trial was rewarded raises dev precision to 0.96 (F1 0.80, mass recall 0.79). Unrewarded-previous a1->S2 D2 steps fire less often and more weakly. The remaining ~19% of mass is at GO when the agent is about to choose a1, early in the episode, often when switching from a2 (prev_action == 2). Adding that as a second clause raised mass recall to 0.88 but lowered F1 to 0.78, so it was left out. The recorded predicate uses only observed variables: at D2 the choice and reached state are inputs, the previous reward was seen at D1, and episode time can be tracked internally. The highest activations, in the top quartile, are covered 92% of the time.
